newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes steady, Aug grade business fading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes steady, Aug grade business fading.

text.p: Outright prices for U.S. cash crudes steadied in an uneventful Thursday morning session, while August grade barrels witnessed mild fluctuations.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing tracked the NYMEX screen, and was talked around even from Wednesday at $19.60-70 a barrel.
Traders said the August/September WTI/Cushing roll rested around a 27 cents discount, putting August benchmark crudes at $19.30-40 a barrel.

Little in the way of closed deals were confirmed, but traders gauged August Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at flat to six cents over WTI marker crude, down slightly from last deals recorded on Wednesday.
Other numbers discussed had West Texas Sour/Midland selling steady to weaker at a $1.60 discount against August WTI, and Eugene Island barrels offered at a $1.35 under WTI.
August Postings Plus business was stuck at $1.73-75, and Midland/WTI at 30-27 cents below WTI/Cushing.
Friday marks the last session for completing August grae business ahead of pipeline scheduling.
